column2: 4.    Subject  to  the  provisions  of  this  Act  and  any  other

column1: written law, the Corporation shall have the power to —

column2: acquire, hold, take or give on lease or hire, mortgage,
pledge,  sell,  exchange,  or  otherwise  alienate,
encumber  or  dispose  of,  any  immovable  property
for the purpose of the Corporation ;
enter into and perform or carry out, whether directly
or  through  any  officer  or  agent  authorized  in  that
behalf  by  the  Corporation,  all  such  contracts  or
agreements as may be necessary for the attainment
of the objects or the exercise of the powers of the
Corporation  ;
accept  gifts,  donations  and  bequests  in  cash  or  in
kind ;
invest its funds, create and administer Trusts and to
maintain current deposits and savings accounts in
any bank ;
publish  or  cause  to  be  published  books,  journals,
magazines  and  other  literature  and  establish  and
maintain libraries, bookshops and printing presses;
advance  or  lend  and  to  borrow  money  for  the
purposes  of  the  Corporation  in  such  manner  and
upon  such  security  as  the  Corporation  may  think
fit; and
appoint,  employ,  transfer,  exercise  disciplinary
control  over  and  dismiss  officers  and  servants
required for the carrying out of the objects of the
Corporation  and  to    prescribe  their  terms  and
conditions of services.
